rationale: An energy-service archetype measured per GJ of output uses 100/efficiency GJ of energy per GJ of output: the two are one quantity stated two ways.

The same identity read the other way. OFF 2026-09-30: on its first run it gave a 7% motor efficiency, 154% for the methane reformer (range to 10,700%) and 183% for a simple-cycle turbine. A pooled specific-energy-consumption with no carrier is not reliably the TOTAL input per GJ of output (UKERC measure rows, examples that give only one carrier), so its inverse is not an efficiency. Turn on per archetype only after checking what the SEC counts.

formula: sum over fossil carriers of specific-energy-consumption(carrier) x CO2 emission factor(carrier)
rationale: Fuel burned times its carbon content. Only where the archetype names the fossil carrier its energy use is in (a carrier-specific specific-energy-consumption), and never where fuel may also be a feedstock (reformers, gasifiers, reactors) or where process emissions are recorded, since a feedstock share would then be counted twice or in the wrong column. Scope 1: electricity and biomass carry no factor.
Total scope-1 emissions are combustion plus process emissions; filled only where both are recorded for the same species and the total is not.

formula: host archetype capex (pooled) + median incremental capex of the set-aside examples
rationale: An incremental cost (the cost of adding a measure or retrofit to an existing plant) is not the archetype's own absolute cost. Adding the pooled cost of the host plant the measure is added to gives one, but the host value comes from other sources, plants and years than the increment, so the result is estimated, not sourced. Only where the archetype has no sourced value, the host is named in host-archetype.csv, and both are on the same unit.
